Committing a real-shape corpus of at least five shape families with real inputs and expected outputs before red ensures every rule is grounded in testable cases before code is written. Converting the corpus into test rows guarantees the suite fails red first against real-world complexities rather than toy examples. Because the expected outputs are defined upfront and measured for stability, the resulting assertions directly catch domain violations without passing bad state. Notes: ensure the red stage strictly verifies row failure before green, and verify that corpus rows are evaluated independently to prevent early assertion exits from masking regressions across families.
